verifications.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:5e819f7a579dbf98eb78f7f8e326a7ad57d939ed6a0762e3bea912f6dc735ed6 (source 3c8b9a3acfe657348249feb297b52cf208324a07). I read the finding in full in findings.json and in the round-4 release-auditor sidecar.
(1) The audit's round-4 probe was re-run UNEDITED on this candidate, on a real API with a disposable PostgreSQL 16 migrated 0001-0130 (production-initialized). It finds 'served strings naming DG0-DG7: 0' and exits 0; round 4 found 24 (30-f990-served-probes.log).
That probe's own 400s (the bare service-identities list and getProcedureDefinition called by id) hid two endpoint families, so I wrote an extended probe. It adds the service identities WITH organizationId, every identity's detail, and getProcedureDefinition by code for the current version and for BOTH seeded configuration versions (versionId 0069 v1 and 0095 v2). Every served string is tested with the product rule itself (mentionsEngineeringGate, the 0089 mirror) and with the audit regex. Result (run 3, 30c): 101 endpoints, all 200; 5322 strings; 0 gate hits, 0 audit-regex hits, 0 internal-reference hits; exit 0.
Runs 1 and 2 (30, 30b) failed on my probe's own wrong call shapes. Run 1 called the detail by id, run 2 used the parameter name 'configVersionId' instead of 'versionId'. Both are disclosed; neither is a product defect.
(2) Mutant M1 reverts the fix: migration 0130 is removed from the clone.
- The shipped seeded-texts scan fails: test 1 gets 142 hits; test 2 finds no reword audit; test 4 cannot find the reword file.
- The unedited audit probe finds 24 again.
- With 0130 restored, the same files pass 5/5 and the probe finds 0 (32-, 33-mutant logs). The fix is what the tests see.
(3) Migration 0130 reviewed line by line, plus an adversarial upgrade probe (31b, 2/2 pass): 0130 applied as an UPGRADE over a demo-initialized database at 0129.
- A job description an administrator changed is left alone: no version step, no audit event.
- A seeded job that an administrator had stepped to version 2 is reworded to version 3, with exactly one audit event (prior 2, new 3, the exact {from, to}).
- A job service identity a person changed (updated_by set) is left alone.
- service_identity_change keeps the old reason and gains the new one at the new record_version (append-only).
- Re-applying the SQL adds 0 audit events (exact-match guards).
- Audit counts: 17/3/4/12/48, plus the two untouched rows, matching the 17/3/5/12/49 of the fresh path.
- On the demo-initialized database every remaining gate-rule hit is history: audit 'from' values, service_identity_change, and the five D-239 audit reasons. One more hit is the gate-submission snapshot note 'unrelated to the engineering delivery gates DG0-DG7', a DG2 disclaimer that D-165 accepted (API data no screen renders) and that is listed in REPORTED_EXISTING_FINDINGS.
(4) I accept the D-239 ruling. The five audit_event.reason texts are append-only audit history (0003/ADR-0004); rewriting them would break a stronger invariant. They state no gate status and tie no G1-G6 to DG0-DG7. The scan admits them only by exact text.
One precision: D-239 says they 'do not name a DG0-DG7 gate', but the product's own rule does match their task ids (T-DG5-ARCH-02 contains 'DG5-'), as the scan's own header says. That is a wording point in the decision record, not a defect.
The new scan (d) covers every text, array and JSON column of every public table, so a new seeded column is scanned automatically. Its non-vacuity case passed in the mutant.
